Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.q: According to the passage, ancient Egyptians gave the world knowledge in ____.
Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.e: The passage says our ancestors gave the world knowledge in writing, mathematics, and medicine.

Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.q: According to the passage, the hieroglyphs carved into temple walls were ____.
o: a list of goods for trade
Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.e: The passage says hieroglyphs were not just beautiful art; they were a way to record history.

Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.q: What made Egypt a center of learning in the past?
Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.e: The Library of Alexandria gathered knowledge from all over the world, making Egypt a center of learning.

Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.q: "Egypt was also a crossroads for trade." This means Egypt was ____.
o: a country with many crossing roads
a place where traders and ideas met
a land closed to other nations
a place where merchants often fought
Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.e: The passage explains that Egypt was a bridge where people met and exchanged ideas.

Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.q: "Our cities rise with modern buildings, while our historical monuments still stand with pride." The word "monuments" means ____.
Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.e: Monuments are historical buildings or structures of importance, like the Pyramids.

Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.q: According to the passage, every citizen's role includes ____.
Taking Pride in Our Beloved Egypt.e: The passage says every citizen has a role: protecting our heritage, contributing to the economy, and sharing our culture.

Moments That Shaped Us.q: Choose the suitable word: Workers are ____ the old mosque so that it looks as it did centuries ago.
Moments That Shaped Us.e: Restoring means repairing an old building so it returns to its original condition.

Moments That Shaped Us.q: Choose the suitable word: Our language, history and traditions form our national ____.
Moments That Shaped Us.e: National identity is who we are as a nation, shaped by our language, history and traditions.

Moments That Shaped Us.q: Choose the suitable word: The museum ____ ancient objects so that future generations can see them.
Moments That Shaped Us.e: To preserve something is to protect it and keep it safe for the future.

Moments That Shaped Us.q: Choose the suitable word: The temples of Luxor are part of the ____ we received from our ancestors.
Moments That Shaped Us.e: Heritage is the history and culture passed down to us from our ancestors.

Moments That Shaped Us.q: Choose the suitable word: Egyptians feel deep ____ when they see their ancient monuments.
Moments That Shaped Us.e: Pride is the good feeling we have about our country and its great achievements.

Moments That Shaped Us.q: In the speaking task, which useful phrase is used to give an example?
Moments That Shaped Us.e: "For example..." introduces an example; the other phrases agree, disagree politely, or add a suggestion.

Now Starts Long Ago.q: While I ____ to school, I met my old teacher.
Now Starts Long Ago.e: The past continuous shows a longer action in progress when a shorter past action happened.

Now Starts Long Ago.q: At 9 o'clock last night, my sister ____ her homework.
Now Starts Long Ago.e: We use the past continuous for an action in progress at a certain time in the past.

Now Starts Long Ago.q: The ancient Egyptians ____ huge temples thousands of years ago.
Now Starts Long Ago.e: The past simple is used for completed past actions, especially with "ago".

Now Starts Long Ago.q: ____ the film, my little brother fell asleep.
Now Starts Long Ago.e: "During" has the meaning of "while", but it is followed by a noun, such as "the film".

Now Starts Long Ago.q: While ____ a book, I heard a strange noise.
Now Starts Long Ago.e: When there is no subject after "while", it is followed by verb + -ing.

Now Starts Long Ago.q: At that time, my grandfather ____ a small farm near the Nile.
Now Starts Long Ago.e: "Have" meaning "possess" is a stative verb, so it is not used in the continuous form.

Where Pride Begins.q: Why does the writer compare pride to a tree?
o: It appears suddenly in a single day.
It gives shade to every visitor.
It grows slowly from strong roots.
It can be cut down very easily.
Where Pride Begins.e: The passage says pride grows slowly, like a tree, from strong roots of history, culture, and shared values.

Where Pride Begins.q: According to the passage, true pride is built through ____.
o: wealth, power and many modern buildings only
forgetting the past and living for today
copying the cultures of other countries
links with the past and duty to the future
Where Pride Begins.e: The writer says true pride is built through connection to the past and responsibility for the future.

Where Pride Begins.q: The achievements of ancient Egyptians in writing, mathematics and medicine became ____.
Where Pride Begins.e: The passage says these achievements were not only for Egypt; they became gifts to the entire world.

Where Pride Begins.q: Egypt gained respect and admiration from other civilizations because it was ____.
o: a home for creativity and expression
the richest trading country in the world
a land with the strongest armies
the only country with a great river
Where Pride Begins.e: Egypt's role as a home for creativity and expression gave it respect and admiration from other civilizations.

Where Pride Begins.q: In "the magnificent temples along the Nile", the word "magnificent" means ____.
Where Pride Begins.e: Magnificent describes something very large, beautiful and impressive, like the temples along the Nile.

Where Pride Begins.q: According to the writer, pride is about what we have inherited and also ____.
o: what we buy from other nations
what other people say about us
what we forget from our past
what we create for the future
Where Pride Begins.e: The passage says pride is not only about what we have inherited, but also about what we create for coming generations.

An Essay about Technology.q: The thesis statement of an essay is ____.
o: the last sentence of the essay
the main idea of the essay
a list of examples and facts
the title written at the top
An Essay about Technology.e: The book defines the thesis statement as the main idea of the essay, presented in the introduction.

An Essay about Technology.q: Which of these belongs in the conclusion, not the introduction?
An Essay about Technology.e: The conclusion summarizes the main points, restates the thesis and gives a final thought or call to action.

An Essay about Technology.q: Each body paragraph should begin with a ____ that states its main idea.
An Essay about Technology.e: A body paragraph includes a topic sentence, which is the main idea of the paragraph.

An Essay about Technology.q: The book compares an essay to a journey. In this comparison, the conclusion is ____.
An Essay about Technology.e: The introduction is where we start, the body paragraphs are the steps, and the conclusion is where we arrive.

An Essay about Technology.q: Which sentence is the best hook for an essay about technology?
o: In conclusion, we must use technology wisely.
This essay has three different paragraphs.
Can you imagine a day without a phone?
Technology is a word with ten letters.
An Essay about Technology.e: A hook grabs the reader's attention with an interesting fact, question or quote.

An Essay about Technology.q: In the reading essay, which paragraph should come right after the introduction?
o: "In conclusion, reading is not just a way..."
"Everyone should try to make reading a regular habit..."
An Essay about Technology.e: The first body paragraph begins with "First"; "Another" comes next, and "In conclusion" ends the essay.

The Warm Bread.q: Why was Sama having a difficult week?
o: She had moved to a new city.
Her neighbour was rude to her.
She had lost her cousin's books.
The Warm Bread.e: The story says her grades were slipping and she felt overwhelmed by her schoolwork.

The Warm Bread.q: "Her grades were slipping." This means her grades were ____.
The Warm Bread.e: If grades slip, they become lower or worse than before.

The Warm Bread.q: "the grey sky that seemed to mirror her mood" means the sky ____.
o: looked as sad as she felt
The Warm Bread.e: The grey sky matched Sama's sad, heavy mood.

The Warm Bread.q: "She hadn't spoken to many people lately and felt isolated." The word "isolated" means ____.
The Warm Bread.e: Sama had little contact with her friends, so she felt alone and cut off from them.

The Warm Bread.q: When her cousin's face lit up, Sama was filled with ____.
The Warm Bread.e: The story says seeing her cousin's face light up filled her with optimism, a hopeful feeling.

The Warm Bread.q: What lesson did Sama learn at the end of the story?
o: Kindness changes your own heart, too.
Fresh bread is the best gift of all.
Grades are not important at all.
Neighbours should visit each other daily.
The Warm Bread.e: Sama realized kindness doesn't just make others feel better; it can change your own heart, too.

Planting Trees, Growing Myself.q: Choose the suitable word: The farmers planted hundreds of ____ along the new road.
Planting Trees, Growing Myself.e: Saplings are young trees, so they can be planted along a road.

Planting Trees, Growing Myself.q: A person who works without pay to help others is a ____.
Planting Trees, Growing Myself.e: The lesson defines a volunteer as a person who works without pay to help others.

Planting Trees, Growing Myself.q: Choose the suitable word: After a year of hard work, the empty land was ____ into a green park.
Planting Trees, Growing Myself.e: Transformed means completely changed in a positive way.

Planting Trees, Growing Myself.q: Choose the suitable word: Speaking in front of the class every week helped me build my ____.
Planting Trees, Growing Myself.e: Confidence is belief in your own abilities, which grows with practice.

Planting Trees, Growing Myself.q: Choose the suitable word: The whole ____ came together to clean the streets of our village.
Planting Trees, Growing Myself.e: A community is people who live in the same area or have something in common.

Planting Trees, Growing Myself.q: Which phrase from the speaking task helps you talk about how volunteering made you feel?
Planting Trees, Growing Myself.e: "It helped me feel..." is the phrase for describing your feelings after helping others.

Voluntary Work.q: Drivers ____ stop at a red light. It's the law.
Voluntary Work.e: We use "must" for rules and laws.

Voluntary Work.q: You ____ use your phone in the exam room. It is not allowed.
You look tired. You ____ go to bed early tonight.
Voluntary Work.e: We use "should" for suggestions and advice.

Voluntary Work.q: I ____ wear a uniform at work. My manager says so.
Voluntary Work.e: We use "have to" when there is no choice; with "I" we say "have to", not "has to".

o: You must to wear a helmet.
Voluntary Work.e: A modal verb is followed by the base form of the verb without "to".

o: rules and laws made by the government
actions we have no choice about
Voluntary Work.e: The book says we use should/shouldn't for suggestions and advice.

Serving the Community in Times of Danger.q: Where does Radwan work as a firefighter?
Serving the Community in Times of Danger.e: Radwan says, "I work as a firefighter in Alexandria."

o: sell fire safety tools in big shops
Serving the Community in Times of Danger.e: Radwan says they rescue people from car accidents, help during floods and save trapped animals.

Serving the Community in Times of Danger.q: Why do firefighters do such risky work?
o: They enjoy dangerous adventures very much.
They are forced to do it by the police.
They want to become famous on television.
They believe in the duty to help others.
Serving the Community in Times of Danger.e: Radwan says they do it because they believe in obligation, the duty to help each other.

Serving the Community in Times of Danger.q: Which word means "a sudden, dangerous situation"?
Serving the Community in Times of Danger.e: An emergency is a sudden, dangerous situation that needs quick action.

Serving the Community in Times of Danger.q: In every emergency, firefighters must act quickly, stay calm and ____.
Serving the Community in Times of Danger.e: Radwan says they must act quickly, stay calm, and trust their training.

Serving the Community in Times of Danger.q: The word "risky" in "our work can be risky" means ____.
Serving the Community in Times of Danger.e: Risky means dangerous; Radwan describes smoke, heat and shaking ladders.

Show, Don't Just Tell.q: According to the lesson, writing a descriptive essay is like ____.
o: writing a long list of numbers and dates
Show, Don't Just Tell.e: The book says a descriptive essay is like painting a picture, but with words instead of paint.

Show, Don't Just Tell.q: Fresh flowers and food cooking are details for the sense of ____.
Show, Don't Just Tell.e: The book lists fresh flowers, salty air and food cooking as examples of smell.

Show, Don't Just Tell.q: Words like soft, rough, cold and warm describe the sense of ____.
Show, Don't Just Tell.e: The book gives soft, rough, cold and warm as examples of what you feel by touch.

Show, Don't Just Tell.q: Which sentence shows sadness instead of just telling it?
o: The girl was sad and she felt very unhappy.
She was a sad girl on a very sad day.
The girl was really, really sad that day.
Her eyes filled with tears as she sobbed.
Show, Don't Just Tell.e: Showing uses descriptive details, like tears and sobbing, so the reader feels the sadness.

Show, Don't Just Tell.q: In a descriptive essay, each body paragraph should focus on ____.
o: the same idea as the introduction
a summary of the whole essay
a new story with new characters
Show, Don't Just Tell.e: The book says each body paragraph should focus on a different aspect or sense.
The book defines adverbs as words that describe actions.

When Appearances Lie.q: In the passage, "wolves in sheep's clothing" are people who ____.
o: love animals and take care of them
are always honest with their friends
When Appearances Lie.e: The passage describes people who put on a friendly face but are not truly honest.

When Appearances Lie.q: According to the passage, dishonest people may deceive us to gain ____.
o: fame and attention on social media sites
When Appearances Lie.e: The passage says they may deceive us to gain money, favors, or private information.

When Appearances Lie.q: Which of these is a warning sign mentioned in the passage?
o: The person gives you time to think.
The story stays the same when you ask.
The promises seem too good to be true.
The platform asks for no personal data.
When Appearances Lie.e: The warning signs include pressure to act quickly, changing stories and promises that seem too good to be true.

When Appearances Lie.q: The advice "Trust, but verify" means we should ____.
o: share every story we read online
When Appearances Lie.e: The passage advises us to pause, ask careful questions and confirm facts from reliable sources.

When Appearances Lie.q: "Another might spread false stories to damage someone's reputation." "Reputation" means ____.
o: the job someone does every day
When Appearances Lie.e: A reputation is the opinion people have about someone; false stories can damage it.

When Appearances Lie.q: What is the writer's final message?
o: Dishonesty shouldn't stop us trusting good people.
We should stop making new friends.
It is better to stay away from the internet forever.
When Appearances Lie.e: The writer says dishonesty should never stop us from believing in the goodness of people.

Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.q: In the speaking role-play, the student who explains the problem plays the role of the ____.
Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.e: One student plays the "friend in trouble" and the other plays the "adviser".

Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.q: After the friend explains the situation, the adviser should first ____.
o: give up and change the subject very quickly
ask questions to understand the problem
tell the friend to stop talking
switch roles with the friend at once
Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.e: The steps say the adviser asks questions, such as "How do you feel about this?", to understand the problem.

Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.q: How many pieces of practical advice should the adviser give at least?
Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.e: The adviser gives at least two pieces of practical advice to help the friend avoid being exploited.

Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.q: Which useful phrase from the lesson warns a friend that something is suspicious?
o: That sounds like a red flag...
One way to protect yourself is...
Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.e: A "red flag" is a warning sign, so this phrase points out that something is suspicious.

Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.q: Which useful phrase is a polite question that suggests an idea?
o: That sounds like a red flag because...
One way to protect yourself is...
Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.e: "Have you considered...?" is the only useful phrase written as a question.

Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.q: Choose the correct advice: A stranger online asks for your personal information. You ____ give it to him.
Wise Choices in a World Full of Traps.e: We use "shouldn't" for advice; sharing personal information with a stranger is unsafe.

Fake Appearance.e: The zero conditional (If + present simple, present simple) is used for scientific facts.

Fake Appearance.q: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ at home.
Fake Appearance.e: The first conditional (If + present simple, will + infinitive) shows a real future possibility.

Fake Appearance.q: If I ____ a lot of money, I would build a hospital.
Fake Appearance.e: The second conditional uses If + past simple, would + infinitive.

Fake Appearance.q: If I ____ you, I would study harder.
Fake Appearance.e: In the second conditional we use the past simple; with "I" the book uses "were": If I were a famous singer...

Fake Appearance.q: We use the second conditional to talk about ____.
Fake Appearance.e: The book says the second conditional is for talking about impossible dreams.

Fake Appearance.q: Which sentence states a general truth correctly?
o: If you mix red and blue, you get purple.
If you mixed red and blue, you get purple.
If you mix red and blue, you would get purple.
If you will mix red and blue, you get purple.
Fake Appearance.e: General truths use the zero conditional: If + present simple, present simple.

The Truth Trap.q: Instead of bullets and bombs, the "war of the new generation" uses ____.
The Truth Trap.e: The passage says this new war uses words: lies, half-truths, and rumors.

The Truth Trap.q: In this kind of war, the main goal is to damage ____.
The Truth Trap.e: The passage says the goal is not to destroy buildings, but to damage trust.

The Truth Trap.q: According to the passage, a rumor about a company can ____.
o: make customers stop buying its products
make the company grow much bigger and richer
help the company find new workers
make its products cheaper to buy
The Truth Trap.e: The passage says a rumor about a company can cause customers to stop buying its products.

The Truth Trap.q: Why is it hard to fight back against this invisible weapon?
o: The truth always spreads faster than lies.
People always check stories before sharing.
A lie online can travel faster than truth.
Lies cannot be shared on social media.
The Truth Trap.e: Once a lie is shared online, it can travel faster than the truth.

o: a true report checked by experts
a weapon used by modern armies
a lesson taught in history books
a story that may not be true
The Truth Trap.e: A rumor is a story that may not be true, passed from person to person.

The Truth Trap.q: Before believing or sharing a story, the writer advises us to ask ____.
o: how many people have liked and shared it
how quickly we can share it
The Truth Trap.e: The writer suggests asking where the information came from and whether it is supported by facts.

Essay Writing Development Plan.q: In the essay outline, "Can a single sentence start a war?" is used as ____.
Essay Writing Development Plan.e: The outline says to start the introduction with a hook, such as a strong question.

Essay Writing Development Plan.q: The thesis statement in the introduction should ____.
o: ask the reader a funny question
give a list of all your sources
end the essay with a call to action
Essay Writing Development Plan.e: The outline says the thesis statement states your main argument clearly.

Essay Writing Development Plan.q: "Furthermore, misinformation can harm entire communities or countries." This sentence is a ____.
Essay Writing Development Plan.e: It introduces the main idea of Body Paragraph 2, so it is a topic sentence.

Essay Writing Development Plan.q: In the conclusion, you should restate the thesis ____.
Essay Writing Development Plan.e: The outline says to summarize your main argument in different words.

Essay Writing Development Plan.q: In the "Two Stars and a Wish" method, the "wish" is ____.
o: one thing you really like a lot
one thing that could be improved
a word that is used very well
the title of your partner's essay
Essay Writing Development Plan.e: The wish suggests one thing that could be improved, such as a clearer thesis.

Essay Writing Development Plan.q: "Therefore, we must all learn to use our words responsibly." This sentence is ____.
Essay Writing Development Plan.e: The conclusion ends with a reflection or a call to action, like this sentence.

Review 1.q: The old and new buildings stand in harmony. The synonym of "harmony" is ____.
Review 1.e: Harmony means things fit well together, so its synonym is agreement.

Review 1.q: She ____ her arm when she fell off her bike.
Review 1.e: Two completed past actions are both in the past simple.

Review 1.q: We ____ dinner when the phone rang.
Review 1.e: The past continuous shows a longer action interrupted by a shorter one in the past simple.

Review 1.q: What ____ you do if you saw a fire in your street?
Review 1.e: The second conditional uses If + past simple with would + infinitive.

Review 1.q: Children ____ play with matches. It's dangerous.
He felt ____ when his close friend told everyone his secret.
Review 1.e: Betrayed describes how you feel when someone you trust lets you down.

Review 1.q: In the reading passage, e-scooters run on ____.
Review 1.e: The passage says these small vehicles run on rechargeable batteries.

Review 1.q: Where is the thesis statement usually found in an essay?
o: at the start of the conclusion
in the middle of every body paragraph
at the end of the introduction
Review 1.e: The thesis statement is usually found at the end of the introduction.

Go Green.q: According to the passage, the Industrial Revolution damaged the environment through pollution and ____.
o: planting too many trees in cities
Go Green.e: The passage says damage came through air and water pollution and the overuse of natural resources.

Go Green.q: According to the passage, "going green" means ____.
o: painting all factories and machines green
living and working in eco-friendly ways
stopping the use of all technology
Go Green.e: Going green means changing the way people live and work so their actions are environmentally friendly.

Go Green.q: Green manufacturing means producing goods in ways that ____.
Go Green.e: The passage defines green manufacturing as producing goods in ways that do not harm the environment.

o: something that can be replaced naturally
a reduction in the amount of something
a large building used as a factory
Go Green.e: Depletion is the reduction in the number or amount of something, like natural resources.

Go Green.q: Recycling and reusing materials reduces the amount of waste going into ____.
Go Green.e: The passage says this approach reduces the amount of waste going into landfills.

Go Green.q: Why are many manufacturers now changing their factories into eco-friendly plants?
o: because it is always cheap and easy
Go Green.e: Global warming, a negative outcome of the Industrial Revolution, is why many manufacturers are going green.

One Bag at a Time.q: Choose the suitable word: Bring a ____ bottle to school instead of buying a new one every day.
One Bag at a Time.e: Reusable means it can be used again many times.

One Bag at a Time.q: Choose the suitable word: Our school started a ____ to collect old clothes for poor families.
One Bag at a Time.e: A campaign is a planned series of activities to achieve a goal.

One Bag at a Time.q: Choose the suitable word: Can we ____ seats? I can't see the board from here.
One Bag at a Time.e: To swap means to exchange one thing for another.

One Bag at a Time.q: Choose the suitable word: Turning off the tap helps ____ the amount of water we use.
One Bag at a Time.e: To reduce means to make something smaller or less.

One Bag at a Time.q: Choose the suitable word: Plastic bags create a lot of ____ that harms the environment.
One Bag at a Time.e: Waste is unwanted or unused material.

o: easy to throw away after one use
One Bag at a Time.e: Reusable describes something that can be used again many times, like a cloth bag.

Small Actions Can Make a Difference.q: My brother enjoys ____ football with his friends.
Small Actions Can Make a Difference.e: "Enjoy" is followed by the -ing form, as in "Sama enjoys reading short stories".
"Decide" is followed by to + infinitive, as in "Joury decided to eat fish".

o: We avoid to eat junk food.
We avoid to eating junk food.

Small Actions Can Make a Difference.q: Which verb can be followed by to + infinitive or -ing with no change in meaning?
Small Actions Can Make a Difference.e: The book lists love, like, hate, prefer, start, begin and continue as taking both forms with no change.

Small Actions Can Make a Difference.q: Please remember ____ off the lights before you leave.
Small Actions Can Make a Difference.e: "Remember to do" is used for something you must not forget to do.

Helping Our Community.q: What was the Water Team's mission?
o: to survey the school's water sources
to plant trees in the playground
to sell cold water bottles to students
Helping Our Community.e: The text says their mission was to survey the school's water sources.

Helping Our Community.q: What was the Water Team's first task?
o: to check for drips or leaks
Helping Our Community.e: Their first task was to check for any drips or leaks.

Helping Our Community.q: What did the team notice about how water was used?
o: The lab sinks were too small to use.
Helping Our Community.e: They noticed some taps were left running while students washed their hands or filled bottles.

Helping Our Community.q: Where did the Water Team present their findings?
Helping Our Community.e: After two weeks, they presented their findings at the school assembly.

Helping Our Community.q: Which idea for saving water did the team share?
o: using water bottles, not paper cups
washing hands only once a week
Helping Our Community.e: They suggested turning off taps completely and using water bottles instead of paper cups.

Helping Our Community.q: What does the story teach about small actions?
o: Many small changes have a big impact.
Only adults can protect the environment.
Saving water is the job of the government.
Helping Our Community.e: The story proved that small changes, made by many people, can have a big impact.

Formal Email Writing.q: Which greeting is suitable for a formal email?
Formal Email Writing.e: The book gives "Dear Sir / Madam," and "Dear Mr. Ali," as formal greetings.

Formal Email Writing.q: Which closing is suitable for a formal email?
Formal Email Writing.e: The book gives "Yours sincerely," and "Kind regards," as formal closings.

Formal Email Writing.q: The language of a formal email should be ____.
o: full of slang and short forms
Formal Email Writing.e: The book says formal email language is polite, in complete sentences, with no slang.

Formal Email Writing.q: A formal email usually states its purpose with ____.
Formal Email Writing.e: The formal template says: "I am writing to [state your purpose clearly]."

Formal Email Writing.q: Which of these is a purpose of a formal email?
o: inviting a cousin to a picnic
Formal Email Writing.e: The book lists job applications, complaints and official requests as purposes of formal emails.

Formal Email Writing.q: Which sentence is the correct formal way to write "I wanna apply for the job"?
o: I wanna apply for this job, okay?
Hey, I'm gonna apply for the job!
I would like to apply for the job.
Me want apply for the job, please.
Formal Email Writing.e: Formal emails use polite, complete sentences and avoid slang like "wanna".

Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.q: According to the passage, if students learn a new language, they will be able to ____.
o: talk to people from other countries
Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.e: The passage says they will be able to communicate with people from different countries.

Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.q: Understanding other cultures promotes respect, ____ and a broader worldview.
Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.e: The passage says understanding other cultures promotes respect, tolerance, and a broader worldview.

o: the ability to speak a language easily
Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.e: The lesson defines tolerance as willingness to accept differences.

Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.q: Why do some students hesitate to learn another language?
o: Their schools do not allow it.
They feel it is too difficult.
They do not like travelling at all.
Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.e: The passage says some feel it is too difficult or time-consuming.

Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.q: If students practiced speaking regularly, they ____ their confidence and fluency.
Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.e: This is the second conditional: If + past simple, would + infinitive.

Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.q: According to the passage, students who speak multiple languages have more opportunities for ____.
Why Learning a Foreign Language Matters.e: The passage says they would have more opportunities for higher education and careers in international companies.

My Journey as a Multilingual.e: "Some" is used in offers and requests.

My Journey as a Multilingual.q: There aren't ____ students in the lab now.
Have you got ____ questions about the trip?
My Journey as a Multilingual.e: "Any" is used in questions with plural countable nouns.

My Journey as a Multilingual.q: If I practice English every day, I ____ it fluently.
My Journey as a Multilingual.e: The first conditional uses If + present simple, will + infinitive.

My Journey as a Multilingual.q: If you spoke French, which country ____ you like to visit?
My Journey as a Multilingual.e: The second conditional uses If + past simple, would + infinitive.

My Journey as a Multilingual.q: According to the note in the lesson, "some" is used in ____.
My Journey as a Multilingual.e: The note says "some" is used in affirmative sentences, offers and requests.

Modern Technology and Learning Foreign L.e: "Advice" is uncountable, so it can't take "a/an" or a plural form.
"Much" is used with uncountable nouns like money.

Modern Technology and Learning Foreign L.q: There are only ____ apples in the basket, not enough for all of us.
Modern Technology and Learning Foreign L.e: "A few" is used with plural countable nouns like apples.

Modern Technology and Learning Foreign L.q: Could you put ____ sugar in my tea, please?
Modern Technology and Learning Foreign L.e: "A little" is used with uncountable nouns like sugar.
The book lists information, advice, homework and money as uncountable nouns.

o: I have a news for you.
I have many news for you.
I have some news for you.
I have a few news for you.
Modern Technology and Learning Foreign L.e: "News" is uncountable, so we can't say "a news".

Ramy's Journey with English.q: Where did Ramy travel one summer?
Ramy's Journey with English.e: The passage says he finally flew to Liverpool, England.

Ramy's Journey with English.q: What was Ramy's biggest difficulty when he arrived?
o: He had no money with him.
Ramy's Journey with English.e: The passage says his biggest difficulty was that he couldn't speak English.

Ramy's Journey with English.q: What happened when Ramy tried to order chicken at a restaurant?
o: The waiter refused to serve him.
He paid twice for the same meal.
Ramy's Journey with English.e: The passage says he wanted chicken but accidentally received fish.

Ramy's Journey with English.q: The word "complicated" in "life became more complicated" means ____.
o: easy, simple and clear to everyone
not simple; hard to deal with
Ramy's Journey with English.e: Complicated means not simple and difficult to understand or deal with.

Ramy's Journey with English.q: What did Ramy do on the night he decided to learn English?
o: He watched English films all night.
Ramy's Journey with English.e: He downloaded a language app, practiced basic phrases, and wrote down useful words.

Ramy's Journey with English.q: By the end of the trip, learning English turned Ramy's journey into ____.
Ramy's Journey with English.e: Ramy realized learning English turned his journey from a struggle into an enriching adventure.

Informal Email.q: Which greeting suits an informal email?
Informal Email.e: Informal greetings are friendly and casual, like "Hi Sara," or "Hello John,".

Informal Email.q: A feature of an informal email is the use of ____.
Informal Email.e: The book says informal emails use contractions such as I'll and can't.
Informal closings include "Best wishes,", "See you soon," and "Love,".

Informal Email.q: Which of these is a purpose of an informal email?
Informal Email.e: The book lists chatting, inviting a friend and sharing news as informal purposes.

Informal Email.q: "Kind regards," is a suitable closing for an email to ____.
Informal Email.e: The book gives "Kind regards," as a formal closing, so it suits professional emails, not chats with friends.

Informal Email.q: Which opening line is written in an informal style?
o: I am writing to request some information.
How are you? I just wanted to tell you...
I am writing to apply for the position.
I am writing to complain about the service.
Informal Email.e: The informal template begins with "How are you? I just wanted to...".

The Modern Job Hunt.q: According to the article, traditional ways of finding jobs have given way to ____.
o: walking into offices with a resume
The Modern Job Hunt.e: The article says traditional methods have largely given way to digital platforms and networking strategies.

The Modern Job Hunt.q: Why can your digital footprint make or break your chances?
o: Websites choose the best workers for them.
All jobs are now done online only.
The Modern Job Hunt.e: Employers often screen candidates online before making contact.

The Modern Job Hunt.q: According to the article, many positions are filled through ____.
The Modern Job Hunt.e: The article says many positions are filled through personal connections rather than public job postings.

The Modern Job Hunt.q: The word "generic" in "the same generic resume" means ____.
The Modern Job Hunt.e: Generic means general or plain; not special or specific.

The Modern Job Hunt.q: How do successful job hunters increase their chances of getting noticed?
o: They send the same resume to every company.
They adapt each application to the role.
They apply to only one or two jobs.
They avoid using keywords from the job.
The Modern Job Hunt.e: Successful job hunters modify their applications to each specific role and use keywords from the job description.

The Modern Job Hunt.q: According to the article, what is important for long-term success in a job search?
The Modern Job Hunt.e: Keeping a positive attitude and learning from each experience is important for long-term success.

Job Interview.q: The word "silos" in the lesson means ____.
Job Interview.e: Silos are teams or departments that work in isolation, not sharing information.

Job Interview.q: Choose the suitable word: The sales ____ deals with all customer orders.
Job Interview.e: A department is a section of a company that deals with a specific job.

Job Interview.q: Choose the suitable word: The manager is ____ a new system to save time.
Job Interview.e: Implementing means putting a plan, idea, or system into action.

o: short updates on how things are going
people affected by a company or project
workers who always prefer to work all alone
Job Interview.e: Stakeholders are people or groups who care about or are affected by a company or project.

o: a new trend in an industry
a person who works alone at home
Job Interview.e: A mentor guides and supports someone less experienced.

Job Interview.q: In the STAR method, the letter "A" stands for ____.
Job Interview.e: STAR means Situation, Task, Action and Result; in Action you describe what you did.

Career Decisions.e: We use "an" before a vowel sound; "honest" starts with a vowel sound.

Career Decisions.q: Mount Everest is ____ highest mountain in the world.
Career Decisions.e: We use "the" before superlatives such as "highest".
The book notes we say "He lives in Egypt", not "the Egypt".

Career Decisions.q: Malak has baked a cake. ____ cake is really delicious.
Career Decisions.e: We use "the" to refer to something for the second time.
We use "a" before a consonant sound; "university" begins with a /j/ sound.
We don't use an article before the names of cities like London.

My Resume.q: According to his resume, how much experience does Sami Adel have?
My Resume.e: His professional summary says he has 3+ years of experience.

My Resume.q: As Social Media Manager, Sami increased follower engagement by ____.
My Resume.e: His resume says he increased follower engagement by 45% across all platforms.

My Resume.q: Which university did Sami Adel graduate from?
My Resume.e: The education section shows a Bachelor of Science from Cairo University in 2020.
His degree is a Bachelor of Science in Information Systems.

My Resume.q: In which job did Sami conduct market research?
My Resume.e: As Marketing Assistant he conducted market research and competitor analysis.
Promotional means related to advertising or promoting something to increase sales or public awareness.

Curriculum Vitae (CV).q: According to the tip box, a CV should be ____.
Curriculum Vitae (CV).e: The tip box says to keep it short: 1-2 pages maximum.

Curriculum Vitae (CV).q: In a CV, education should be listed in ____.
Curriculum Vitae (CV).e: The book says to list qualifications in reverse chronological order, most recent first.

Curriculum Vitae (CV).q: The personal statement in a CV is ____.
o: a full story of your childhood years
a long list of your hobbies
Curriculum Vitae (CV).e: The personal statement is a short paragraph (2-3 sentences) describing who you are and what you want.

Curriculum Vitae (CV).q: Communication, teamwork and leadership are examples of ____.
Curriculum Vitae (CV).e: The book lists communication, teamwork and leadership as soft skills.
References are people who can recommend you for a job.

Curriculum Vitae (CV).q: Choose the suitable action verb: She ____ the sales data to find new trends.
Curriculum Vitae (CV).e: "Analyzed" means studied the data in detail, which fits finding trends.

Review 2.q: He admitted ____ the money from the drawer.
There isn't ____ milk in the fridge.
Review 2.e: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns like milk in negative sentences.
We use "an" before a singular noun starting with a vowel sound.

Review 2.q: Choose the suitable word: The company uses ____ energy such as solar and wind power.
Review 2.e: Renewable energy, like solar and wind, can be replaced naturally.

Review 2.q: This phone looks like every other phone. Its design is very ____.
Review 2.e: Generic means general or plain; not special, so it doesn't stand out.

Review 2.q: In the reading passage, Eco-Vision reduced its energy use by ____.
Review 2.e: The passage says Eco-Vision has reduced its energy use by 40%.
Employees join regular check-ins with their teams, which avoids silos and keeps everyone connected.

o: I need a furniture for my flat.
I need many furnitures for my flat.
I need a few furniture for my flat.
I need some furniture for my flat.
Review 2.e: "Furniture" is uncountable, so it takes "some", not "a", "many" or "a few".

Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.q: The younger fishermen called Santiago "salao", which means ____.
o: the oldest man in the village
Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.e: The chapter says they called him salao, the worst kind of unlucky.

Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.q: How old was Manolin when he started fishing with Santiago?
Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.e: The boy had fished with Santiago since he was five; now he was twelve.

Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.q: Santiago's bed in his hut was made of ____.
Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.e: Inside the hut there was a bed made of newspapers and a single blanket.

Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.q: Santiago said, "It is better to be lucky. But I would rather be ____."
Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.e: Santiago wants to be exact so that he is ready when luck comes.

Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.q: Why did Santiago admire Joe DiMaggio?
o: He was the richest player in the team.
He played even with pain in his heel.
He used to be a fisherman like him.
Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.e: Santiago says DiMaggio played even when he had pain in his heel and never gave up.

Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.q: What did Santiago dream of at night?
o: lions on the beaches of Africa
big fish in the Gulf Stream
the Yankees winning a baseball game
Chapter 1: The Old Man and His Luck.e: He dreamed of young lions playing on the beaches of Africa; they meant strength, youth and freedom.

Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.q: In the early morning, Manolin brought Santiago black beans, rice and ____.
Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.e: Manolin said, "Some black beans, rice, and a little coffee."

Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.q: Santiago's sail, patched many times, looked like ____.
Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.e: The chapter says the sail was patched many times and looked like the flag of defeat.

Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.q: Why did Santiago tell Manolin to stay with the other boat?
o: The boy was too young to fish.
Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.e: Santiago replied, "You are with a lucky boat now. Stay with them."

Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.q: In this chapter, Santiago baited his lines with ____.
Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.e: He baited his lines carefully with fresh sardines and lowered them at different depths.

Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.q: Santiago believed that, more than luck, ____ mattered.
o: help from the other young fishermen
Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.e: The chapter says he believed luck was only part of the story; skill, patience, and endurance mattered more.

Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.q: "Where the bird circles, there are fish." This shows that Santiago ____.
o: wants to catch the circling bird
Chapter 2: Preparing for the Great Day.e: Santiago uses his experience: a circling bird tells him fish are near.

Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.q: Why did the small tuna jump into the air?
o: They were chasing the circling bird above.
The water was too hot for them.
They were frightened by something larger.
Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.e: Small tuna jumped, frightened by something larger below.

Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.q: What did Santiago do when the great fish first took the bait?
o: He pulled the line very hard at once.
He let the fish eat without pulling.
He cut the line with his knife.
Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.e: He did not pull; he let the fish eat because he knew the ways of big fish.

Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.q: After the fish was hooked, it ____.
o: pulled the boat out to sea
jumped high out of the water
Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.e: The fish did not jump; it swam steadily out into the open sea, pulling the boat.

Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.q: To take some of the strain, Santiago ____.
o: gave the line to another fishing boat
tied the line across his shoulders
Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.e: He tied the line across his shoulders to take some of the strain, but never let go.

Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.q: Santiago spoke to the fish and called it his ____.
Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.e: He said, "Fish, you are my brother. But I will not let you go."

Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.q: The expression "May the best of us win" shows ____.
o: hope for a quick and easy win
Chapter 3: The Big Fish Bites.e: The chapter's expressions list explains "May the best of us win" as fairness in a struggle.

Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.q: Joe DiMaggio played baseball with ____ in his heel.
Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.e: Santiago thought of DiMaggio, who played baseball with a bone spur in his heel.

Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.q: When the marlin finally leapt, Santiago saw that it was ____.
Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.e: The marlin was enormous, longer than the boat itself, silver in the sunlight.

Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.q: How did Santiago describe the marlin after it leapt?
o: noble, strong and full of spirit
small, thin, weak and very tired
Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.e: He whispered, "Never have I seen such a fish. Noble, strong, and full of spirit."

Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.q: During the long battle, Santiago ate ____.
Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.e: The chapter says he ate little, only raw fish, and drank sparingly from his water bottle.

Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.q: What gave Santiago strength at night when he felt lonely?
Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.e: He remembered the lions of his youth playing on the beaches of Africa; that dream gave him strength.

Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.q: "His body was broken, but his will was like iron." This means Santiago ____.
o: was strong and full of energy
Chapter 4: A Battle of Strength and Will.e: His body was tired and hurt, but his determination stayed very strong.

Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.q: How did Santiago finally kill the marlin?
o: He cut the line and let it swim away.
He drove the harpoon into its heart.
He hit it with the oar many times.
He pulled it into the boat with a net.
Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.e: When the fish came close, he drove the iron deep into its heart.

Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.q: Why did tears fill Santiago's eyes after killing the marlin?
Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.e: Tears filled his eyes, not only from victory but from sorrow for the noble fish.

Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.q: What did Santiago do with the marlin after he killed it?
o: He put it inside his small wooden boat.
He sold it to another fisherman.
He tied it to the side of the skiff.
He let it sink to the bottom.
Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.e: He tied the marlin to the side of his skiff; it was longer than the boat.

Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.q: What danger did Santiago expect on his way home?
Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.e: He knew the smell of blood in the water would call the sharks.

Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.q: Santiago said "Forgive me" to the fish. This shows his ____.
o: wish to stop fishing at sea forever
Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.e: The chapter's values say he asks the fish's forgiveness out of respect for a noble opponent.

Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.q: Why did Santiago think the villagers would not believe him?
o: He had told lies to them before.
No man could take such a fish alone.
The fish was too small to see.
He had no witnesses from his family.
Chapter 5: The Great Marlin Revealed.e: He thought, "They will say no man could take such a fish alone."

Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.q: What kind of shark attacked the marlin first?
Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.e: The first shark was a mako shark, fast and strong, following the trail of blood.

Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.q: The galanos that came next were ____.
Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.e: The chapter calls them galanos, shovel-nosed sharks, slower but insistent.

Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.q: What did Santiago do after his harpoon broke?
o: He gave up and lay down.
He tied his knife to an oar.
He threw the marlin back into the sea.
Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.e: He tied his knife to an oar and used it as a spear.

Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.q: Santiago whispered, "I was beaten, but only by ____."
Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.e: He said, "I was beaten, but only by sharks, not by the fish."

Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.q: By night, what was left of the marlin?
Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.e: The marlin was now only a skeleton, stripped of nearly all its meat.

Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.q: At the end of the chapter, Santiago had lost his catch, but not his ____.
Chapter 6: The Sharks Arrive.e: The chapter says he had lost his catch, but he had not lost his dignity.
